Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)  
- Assessment consistent with lower abdominal pain of gradual onset for 2 days, burning in character, localized below the umbilicus, associated with pink-colored urine (possible hematuria), increased urinary frequency without dysuria, mild nausea, and subjective feeling of being hot and sweaty (no measured fever).  
- The leading diagnosis is urinary tract infection (cystitis) given symptom constellation and planned empiric antibiotic treatment.  
- Differential diagnoses consistent with the transcript include:  
  • Urinary tract infection (High likelihood) – typical symptoms and treatment priority.  
  • Early pregnancy-related complications including ectopic pregnancy (Moderate likelihood) – patient sexually active with Implanon, pregnancy test advised to rule out.  
  • Pelvic inflammatory disease (Moderate likelihood) – considered due to sexual activity and lower abdominal pain; no vaginal symptoms reported which lowers likelihood but cannot be excluded.  
- Other differentials from DDx such as constipation-related pain and Implanon-related complications are less likely and less consistent with clinical presentation.  
- No contradictions noted between transcript and DDx.  

Management Plan  
- Started empiric antibiotic therapy with Trimethoprim (2 tablets total per dose), one tablet twice daily for 3 days.  
- Advised to maintain adequate hydration and use regular Paracetamol for pain relief.  
- Recommended cranberry juice as a supportive measure for urinary symptoms.  
- Planned pregnancy test to exclude pregnancy complications despite contraception use.  
- Patient advised to monitor symptoms and return if worsening pain, fever, vomiting, or other concerning features develop.  
- Follow-up arranged to reassess if symptoms persist or worsen.

- Urinary tract infection (cystitis) – High likelihood; consistent with burning lower abdominal pain, pink urine, urinary frequency, and systemic symptoms.  
- Early pregnancy-related complications (including ectopic pregnancy) – Moderate likelihood; considered due to sexual activity and symptoms; pregnancy test pending to exclude.  
- Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) – Moderate likelihood; sexually active female with constitutional symptoms, but no vaginal discharge or dysuria lowers likelihood.
